pages.text: "I'll move it myself!" Rice bundles stood in rows in the paddy. Dingding hugged the thickest bundle with both hands, wanting to carry it to the bank alone.
Heave-ho! The bundle was taller than Dingding. With one step, it started tipping forward. Dingding's face was buried in straw, and they could not see ahead.
Thump! The bundle fell forward, almost on top of Dingding. Rice ears scattered over the soil. Dingding landed sitting on the ground.
Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, came from the neighboring paddy. "Even I can't lift such a thick bundle alone." Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, came down the bank, too.
Grandma put a hand on one side. "Grandma here." Mom put hers on the other. "Mom here." "Then I'll be in the middle!" Three hands held one bundle.
"One, two, three—lift!" Grandma counted. The bundle rose off the soil. "Three Together—Up It Goes!" Dingding called excitedly.
Matching their steps, all three walked to the bank and stood the bundle upright. Before, Dingding could not take even one step. Now they got there in one trip.
Dingding sniffed the nutty smell of dry straw. "It was heavy alone, but with three of us, it isn't heavy at all!" Grandma tapped Dingding's hand gently.

Now Dingding knew how three could lift together. "One, call for help if it's heavy! Two, gather our hands! Three, lift together!" That evening, when it was time to move the big wooden tub, Dingding called first. "Grandma, Mom! One hand each, please!"
Grandma and Mom hugged Dingding between them. With three hands, even something too heavy for one could rise. "Three Together—Up It Goes!" Dingding raised both hands high.
